Due to that, using any methods that modify the uv value will cause the new uv to treat scaled width and height as true dimensions and can lead to unexpected results if not accounted for.

scrollDiscrete.haxe_doc: Scrolls the texture position by specified amount.

dispose.haxe_doc: Disposes of the Tile and its underlying Texture. Note that if Texture is used by other Tile instances, it will cause them to point at a disposed texture and can lead to errors.

clone.haxe_doc: Create a copy of this Tile instance.

class.haxe_doc:
A core 2D rendering component representing a region of an underlying `h3d.mat.Texture`.
Tiles cannot be created directly, and instances are created with the following methods: * Via the Resource Management system: `hxd.res.Image.toTile`. * From pre-existing Texture: `Tile.fromTexture`. * From pre-existing `BitmapData` or `Pixels`: `Tile.fromBitmap` and `Tile.fromPixels` (as well as `Tile.autoCut`). * From solid color: `Tile.fromColor`. * From previously existing Tile instance via various methods, such as `Tile.sub`.

Clamp.haxe_doc: Uses the pixels of the edge.

Mirror.haxe_doc: Repeats the texture, mirrored every other time.

enum.haxe_doc: How texture coordinates outside of the `[0, 1]` range are handled (see `Texture.wrap`).

ARGB.haxe_doc: 8 bits per channel, bytes in the order alpha, red, green, blue.

BGRA.haxe_doc: 8 bits per channel, bytes in the order blue, green, red, alpha.

RGBA.haxe_doc: 8 bits per channel, bytes in the order red, green, blue, alpha.

SRGB.haxe_doc: 3 channels of 8 bits, in the sRGB color space.

SRGB_ALPHA.haxe_doc: 4 channels of 8 bits, with the colors in the sRGB color space.

RGB10A2.haxe_doc: 10 bits for each color channel and 2 bits for the alpha.

RG11B10UF.haxe_doc: Unsigned floats: 11 bits for red and green, 10 bits for blue.

S3TC.haxe_doc: A block compressed format: `v` is the BC number, from `1` (DXT1) to `7`.

Depth24Stencil8.haxe_doc: A 24 bits depth with an 8 bits stencil.

Depth32Stencil8.haxe_doc: A 32 bits float depth with an 8 bits stencil.

enum.haxe_doc: The pixel formats of textures and `Pixels`: color formats (8 bits, half and full floats per channel), compressed formats (`S3TC`) and depth formats.

TRILINEAR_FILTERING_ENABLED.haxe_doc: If `true`, mipmapped textures are created with `Linear` mip filtering, otherwise `Nearest`.

DEFAULT_WRAP.haxe_doc: The wrap mode of new textures.

getDefaultDepth.haxe_doc: This will return the default depth buffer, which is automatically resized to the screen size.

fromBitmap.haxe_doc: Creates a texture from a bitmap.

fromPixels.haxe_doc: Creates a texture from pixels. @param format The texture format (the pixels format by default).

fromColor.haxe_doc: Creates a 1x1 texture using the RGB color passed as parameter.

genDisc.haxe_doc: Returns a shared `size` x `size` texture with a filled disc of the given color (`0xRRGGBB`).

defaultCubeTexture.haxe_doc: Returns a default dummy 1x1 black cube texture

genChecker.haxe_doc: Returns a checker texture of size x size, than can be repeated

genNoise.haxe_doc: Returns a shared `size` x `size` texture filled with random values.

id.haxe_doc: A unique identifier of the texture.

name.haxe_doc: The texture name (usually its resource path), used for debugging. See `setName`.

width.haxe_doc: The width, in pixels.

height.haxe_doc: The height, in pixels.

flags.haxe_doc: The flags given at creation, and some state flags such as `Loading`.

mipMap.haxe_doc: How the mip levels are sampled (`None` unless the texture is `MipMapped`).

filter.haxe_doc: How the pixels are interpolated (`Linear` by default).

wrap.haxe_doc: How the texture coordinates outside of `[0, 1]` are handled (`DEFAULT_WRAP` by default).

slice.haxe_doc: For texture arrays: if positive, binds only the layer `slice - 1` as a 2D texture (DirectX 12).

layerCount.haxe_doc: The number of layers: 6 for cube textures, the number of layers of texture arrays, the depth of 3D textures, 1 otherwise.

lodBias.haxe_doc: A bias added to the mip level selected when sampling, from -15 to 16: positive values select less detailed levels.

mipLevels.haxe_doc: The number of mip levels (1 if the texture is not `MipMapped`).

anisotropicMaxLevel.haxe_doc: The maximum level of anisotropic filtering (1 to 16).

startingMip.haxe_doc: The most detailed mip level sampled: levels before it are ignored.

residentMip.haxe_doc: The most detailed mip level allocated on the GPU : mip levels before it are not allocated, and the texture is sampled starting at this level.

isPlaceholder.haxe_doc: A 1x1 texture is allocated while the texture is loading (see hxd.res.Image)

realloc.haxe_doc: If this callback is set, the texture can be re-allocated when the 3D context has been lost or when it's been free because of lack of memory.

depthBuffer.haxe_doc: When the texture is used as render target, tells which depth buffer will be used. If set to null, depth testing is disabled.

alloc.haxe_doc: Allocates the GPU memory of the texture if it is not allocated.

isSRGB.haxe_doc: Tells if the format stores sRGB colors.

clone.haxe_doc: Returns a GPU copy of the texture (same size, format and main flags).

preventAutoDispose.haxe_doc: In case we run out of GPU memory, textures that hasn't been used for a long time will be disposed. Calling this will make this texture not considered for auto disposal.

waitLoad.haxe_doc: Some textures might take some time to load. You can check flags.has(Loading) or add a waitLoad callback which will get called either immediately if the texture is already loaded or when loading is complete.

setName.haxe_doc: Sets the texture name, used for debugging.

isDisposed.haxe_doc: Tells if the GPU memory is released and cannot be restored with `realloc`.

resize.haxe_doc: Changes the texture size. The content is lost.

clearF.haxe_doc: Fills a render target with the given float color. @param layer The layer to clear, or `-1` for all layers.

setResidentMip.haxe_doc: Releases the GPU memory of the mip levels more detailed than `mip` (texture streaming). Returns `false` if the driver does not support it. Not supported for render targets and depth textures.

uploadBitmap.haxe_doc: Uploads the pixels of a bitmap to a mip level and layer. The size must match the mip level size.

uploadPixels.haxe_doc: Uploads pixels to a mip level and layer. The size must match the mip level size. Uploading the level 0 of the last layer of a `MipMapped` texture generates the mip levels, unless `ManualMipMapGen` is set.

dispose.haxe_doc: Releases the GPU memory of the texture.

hasStencil.haxe_doc: Tells if the format is a depth format with a stencil.

isDepth.haxe_doc: Tells if the format is a depth format.

getHandle.haxe_doc: Returns the bindless handle of the texture (requires a driver supporting bindless textures).

capturePixels.haxe_doc: Downloads the current texture data from the GPU. Beware, this is a very slow operation that shouldn't be done during rendering.

SOFTWARE_DRIVER.haxe_doc: If `true`, the engine is created with a software driver (set before creating the engine).

ANTIALIASING.haxe_doc: The number of samples of the multisampling antialiasing of the output (set before creating the engine).

id.haxe_doc: The identifier of the engine (with `-D multidriver`).

hardware.haxe_doc: `true` if the driver is hardware accelerated.

width.haxe_doc: The width of the output, in pixels.

height.haxe_doc: The height of the output, in pixels.

debug.haxe_doc: Enables the debug mode of the driver (more checks and error reports, slower).

drawTriangles.haxe_doc: The number of triangles drawn during the last frame.

drawCalls.haxe_doc: The number of draw calls during the last frame.

dispatches.haxe_doc: The number of compute shader dispatches during the last frame.

shaderSwitches.haxe_doc: The number of shader changes during the last frame.

backgroundColor.haxe_doc: The color (`0xAARRGGBB`) the output is cleared with at the beginning of each frame, or `null` to not clear it.

autoResize.haxe_doc: If `true` (default), the output follows the window size.

fullScreen.haxe_doc: Displays the window in full screen (borderless) mode, on platforms with windows.

fps.haxe_doc: The smoothed number of frames rendered per second.

setCurrent.haxe_doc: Makes this engine the current one.

init.haxe_doc: Initializes the driver. `onReady` is called when it is ready. Done by `hxd.App`.

driverName.haxe_doc: Returns the name of the driver (and details such as the GPU name if `details` is set).

selectShader.haxe_doc: Low level: selects the shader used by the next draw calls.

selectMaterial.haxe_doc: Low level: applies the render states of `pass` for the next draw calls.

uploadInstanceShaderBuffers.haxe_doc: Low level: uploads the per-object parameters, textures and buffers of the current shader.

uploadShaderBuffers.haxe_doc: Low level: uploads a kind of shader buffers (globals, parameters, textures or buffers) of the current shader.

renderMultiBuffers.haxe_doc: Low level: draws triangles whose vertex inputs come from several buffers.

renderInstanced.haxe_doc: Low level: draws instances with the given draw commands.

onContextLost.haxe_doc: Called when the GPU context was lost and recreated: GPU resources without `realloc` must be recreated.

onReady.haxe_doc: Called when the driver is initialized.

onResized.haxe_doc: Called after the output was resized to follow the window.

begin.haxe_doc: Starts a frame: resets the statistics and clears the output with `backgroundColor`. Returns `false` if the driver cannot render. Called by `render`.

hasFeature.haxe_doc: Tells if the driver supports the feature `f` (see `h3d.impl.Driver.Feature`).

end.haxe_doc: Ends the frame and presents it. Called by `render`.

getCurrentTarget.haxe_doc: Returns the current render target, or `null` when rendering to the screen.

pushTargets.haxe_doc: Renders to several textures at once (multiple render targets) until the matching `popTarget`.

pushDepth.haxe_doc: Renders only to a depth texture until the matching `popTarget`.

popTarget.haxe_doc: Restores the render target active before the last `pushTarget`.

clearF.haxe_doc: Clears the current target with a float color, and optionally the depth and stencil.

setRenderZone.haxe_doc: * Sets up a scissored zone to eliminate pixels outside the given range. * Call with no parameters to reset to full viewport.

render.haxe_doc: Renders a frame: calls `begin`, `obj.render(this)` and `end`, and updates `fps`. Done every frame by `hxd.App`.

setDepthClamp.haxe_doc: Enables the depth clamping of the next draw calls.

setDepthBias.haxe_doc: Sets the depth bias of the next draw calls (used against shadow acne).

dispose.haxe_doc: Releases the driver and all the GPU resources.

Target.haxe_doc: Allocate a texture that will be used as render target.

Cube.haxe_doc: Allocate a cube texture. Might be restricted to power of two textures only.

MipMapped.haxe_doc: Activates Mip Mapping for this texture. Might not be available for target textures.

ManualMipMapGen.haxe_doc: By default, textures created with MipMapped will have their mipmaps generated when you upload the mipmap level 0. This flag disables this and manually upload mipmaps instead.

IsNPOT.haxe_doc: This is a not power of two texture. Automatically set when having width or height being not power of two.

NoAlloc.haxe_doc: Don't initialy allocate the texture memory.

Dynamic.haxe_doc: Inform that we will often perform upload operations on this texture

AlphaPremultiplied.haxe_doc: Assumes that the color value of the texture is premultiplied by the alpha component.

WasCleared.haxe_doc: Tells if the target texture has been cleared (reserved for internal engine usage).

Loading.haxe_doc: The texture is being currently loaded. Set onLoaded to get event when loading is complete.

Serialize.haxe_doc: Allow texture data serialization when found in a scene (for user generated textures)

IsArray.haxe_doc: Tells if it's a texture array

AsyncLoading.haxe_doc: Allows a DDS texture to be loaded asynchronously (see hxd.res.Image.ASYNC_LOADING)

LazyLoading.haxe_doc: By default, the texture are loaded from images when created. If this flag is enabled, the texture will be loaded from disk when first used.

Writable.haxe_doc: Texture can be written in shaders using RWTexture

enum.haxe_doc: The flags of a `Texture`, given at creation.

Linear.haxe_doc: Interpolates between the two nearest mip levels (trilinear filtering).

enum.haxe_doc: How the mip levels of a texture are sampled (see `Texture.mipMap`).

AnisotropicNearest.haxe_doc: Anisotropic filtering for surfaces seen at grazing angles, nearest pixel otherwise.

AnisotropicLinear.haxe_doc: Anisotropic filtering for surfaces seen at grazing angles, linear otherwise.

enum.haxe_doc: How the pixels of a texture are interpolated when sampled (see `Texture.filter`).

ENGINE_PACKAGES.haxe_doc: The packages skipped to find `position` (`hrt` is the Hide runtime).

make.haxe_doc: Records the current position, or returns `null` if the tracking is disabled.

position.haxe_doc: The first position of the call stack outside of the engine packages (`file:line`).

stack.haxe_doc: The positions of the call stack.

class.haxe_doc: The code position where a GPU resource (buffer, texture) was allocated, recorded to track memory leaks. Enabled with `h3d.impl.MemoryManager.enableTrackAlloc`.

length.haxe_doc: The length of this stack.

callStack.haxe_doc: Return the call stack elements, or an empty array if not available.

exceptionStack.haxe_doc:
Return the exception stack : this is the stack elements between the place the last exception was thrown and the place it was caught, or an empty array if not available. Set `fullStack` parameter to true in order to return the full exception stack.
May not work if catch type was a derivative from `haxe.Exception`.

toString.haxe_doc: Returns a representation of the stack as a printable string.

subtract.haxe_doc: Returns a range of entries of current stack from the beginning to the the common part of this and `stack`.

copy.haxe_doc: Make a copy of the stack.

class.haxe_doc: Do not use manually.

enum.haxe_doc: Elements return by `CallStack` methods.

dom.haxe_doc: The DomKit properties of the object: component, classes, id, state and style.

parent.haxe_doc: The parent object, or `null`.

getChildRefPosition.haxe_doc: Returns the index of the first (or last if `first` is not set) child counting for the `:first-child`, `:last-child`, `:odd` and `:even` CSS pseudo classes.

class.haxe_doc: The base type of the objects of the UI, `T` being the base class of the components: implement it on your base class (with Heaps, `h2d.Object` is used).

x.haxe_doc: The horizontal position of the point.

y.haxe_doc: The vertical position of the point.

distanceSq.haxe_doc: Returns squared distance between this Point and given Point `p`.

distance.haxe_doc: Returns a distance between this Point and given Point `p`.

sub.haxe_doc: Substracts Point `p` from this Point and returns new Point with the result.

add.haxe_doc: Adds Point `p` to this Point and returns new Point with the result.

scaled.haxe_doc: Returns a new Point with the position of this Point multiplied by a given scalar `v`.

equals.haxe_doc: Tests if this Point position equals to `other` Point position.

dot.haxe_doc: Returns a dot product between this Point and given Point `p`.

lengthSq.haxe_doc: Returns squared length of this Point.

length.haxe_doc: Returns length (distance to `0,0`) of this Point.

normalized.haxe_doc: Returns a new Point with the normalized values of this Point.

set.haxe_doc: Sets the Point `x,y` with given values.

load.haxe_doc: Copies `x,y` from given Point `p` to this Point.

clone.haxe_doc: Returns a copy of this Point.

cross.haxe_doc: Returns a cross product between this Point and a given Point `p`.

lerp.haxe_doc: Sets this Point position to a result of linear interpolation between Points `p1` and `p2` at the interpolant position `k`.

transform.haxe_doc: Applies a given Matrix `m` transformation to this Point position.

transformed.haxe_doc: Returns a new Point with a result of applying a Matrix `m` to this Point position.

transform2x2.haxe_doc: Applies a given 2x2 Matrix `m` transformation to this Point position.

transformed2x2.haxe_doc: Returns a new Point with a result of applying a 2x2 Matrix `m` to this Point position.

toIPoint.haxe_doc: Converts this point to integer point scaled by provided scalar `scale` (rounded).

rotate.haxe_doc: Rotates this Point around `0,0` by a given `angle`.

getRotation.haxe_doc: Get the angle in radians between the vector (1, 0) and this Point. The angle returned is [-π, π]

class.haxe_doc: A simple 2D position/vector container. @see `h2d.col.IPoint`

parentContainer.haxe_doc: The parent container of this object. See `Object.contentChanged` for more details.

parent.haxe_doc: The parent object in the scene tree.

numChildren.haxe_doc: How many immediate children this object has.

name.haxe_doc: The name of the object. Can be used to retrieve an object within a tree by using `Object.getObjectByName`.

x.haxe_doc: The x position (in pixels) of the object relative to its parent.

y.haxe_doc: The y position (in pixels) of the object relative to its parent.

scaleX.haxe_doc: The amount of horizontal scaling of this object.

scaleY.haxe_doc: The amount of vertical scaling of this object.

rotation.haxe_doc: The rotation angle of this object, in radians.

visible.haxe_doc: Is the object and its children are displayed on screen.

alpha.haxe_doc: The amount of transparency of the Object.

filter.haxe_doc:
The post process filter for this object.
When set, `Object.alpha` value affects both filter and object transparency (use `Drawable.color.a` to set transparency only for the object).

blendMode.haxe_doc:
The blending mode of the object.
If there is no `Object.filter` active, only applies to the current object (not inherited by children). Otherwise tells how the filter is blended with background.

dom.haxe_doc: The domkit properties of the object (with the `domkit` library), set when it is a domkit component.

posChanged.haxe_doc:
A flag that indicates that the object transform was modified and absolute position recalculation is required.
Automatically cleared on `Object.sync` and can be manually synced with the `Object.syncPos`.

allocated.haxe_doc:
A flag that indicates whether the object was allocated or not.
When adding children to allocated objects, `onAdd` is being called immediately, otherwise it's delayed until the whole tree is added to a currently active `Scene`.

getSize.haxe_doc: Similar to `getBounds(parent)`, but instead of the full content, it will return the size based on the alignment of the object. For instance for a text, `Object.getBounds` will return the full glyphs size whereas `getSize` will ignore the pixels under the baseline. @param out An optional bounds instance to fill. Allocates new Bounds instance and returns it if not set.

getAbsPos.haxe_doc: Returns the updated absolute position matrix. See `Object.getMatrix` for current matrix values.

contains.haxe_doc: Tells if the object is contained into this object children, recursively.

find.haxe_doc: Find a single object in the tree by calling `f` on each and returning the first not-null value returned, or null if not found.

findAll.haxe_doc: Find several objects in the tree by calling `f` on each and returning all the not-null values returned. @param arr An optional array instance to fill results with. Allocates a new array if not set.

getObjectsCount.haxe_doc: Return the total number of children in the whole tree, recursively.

localToGlobal.haxe_doc: Convert a local position (or `[0,0]` if `pt` is null) relative to the object origin into an absolute screen position, applying all the inherited transforms. @param pt An optional position to convert and return. Allocates new Point at 0,0 position if not set. Modifies the Point instance as is.

globalToLocal.haxe_doc: Convert an absolute screen position into a local position relative to the object origin, applying all the inherited transforms. @param pt A position to convert and return. Modifies the Point instance as is.

getScene.haxe_doc: Returns an `h2d.Scene` down the hierarchy tree or `null` if object is not added to Scene.

addChild.haxe_doc: Add a child object at the end of the children list.

addChildAt.haxe_doc: Insert a child object at the specified position of the children list.

onContentChanged.haxe_doc: Should be called when Object content was changed in order to notify parent container. See `Object.contentChanged`.

onAdd.haxe_doc:
Sent when object is being added to an allocated scene.
Do not remove the super call when overriding.

onRemove.haxe_doc:
Sent when object is removed from the allocated scene.
Do not remove the super call when overriding.

getMatrix.haxe_doc: Populates `m` with current absolute object transform values. See `Object.getAbsPos` for up-to-date values.

removeChild.haxe_doc: Remove the given object from the immediate children list of the object if it's part of it.

setParentContainer.haxe_doc: Sets the parent container for this Object and it's children. See `Object.contentChanged` for more details.

removeChildren.haxe_doc: Remove all children from the immediate children list.

remove.haxe_doc: Same as `parent.removeChild(this)`, but does nothing if parent is null.

drawTo.haxe_doc: Draw the object and all its children into the given Texture.

drawToTextures.haxe_doc: Draw the object and all its children into the given Textures.

draw.haxe_doc: Override this method in order to add custom graphics rendering to your Object. `draw` is invoked before rendering of the object children.

sync.haxe_doc:
Performs a sync of data for rendering (such as absolute position recalculation). While this method can be used as a substitute to an update loop, it's primary purpose it to prepare the Object to be rendered.
Do not remove the super call when overriding.

syncPos.haxe_doc: Ensures that object has an up-to-date position transform.

calcAbsPos.haxe_doc: Internal usage Calculates the absolute object position transform. See `Object.syncPos` for a safe position sync method. This method does not ensure that object parents also have up-to-date transform nor does it clear the `Object.posChanged` flag.

emitTile.haxe_doc: Draws single Tile instance with this Object transform.

clipBounds.haxe_doc: Internal usage Clip the local bounds with our global viewport. Used during filter rendering in order to clip out areas that are off-screen and should not be rendered. `h2d.Scene` note: `clipBounds` will always output bounds equivalent to entire window. This is done in order for scene to never clip out cameras as they may render virtually any area of the Scene.

move.haxe_doc: Move the object by the specified amount along its current direction (`Object.rotation` angle).

setPosition.haxe_doc: Set the position of the object relative to its parent.

rotate.haxe_doc: Rotate the object by the given angle (in radians)

scale.haxe_doc: Scale uniformly the object by the given factor.

setScale.haxe_doc: Set the uniform scale for the object.

getChildAt.haxe_doc: Return the `n`th element among the immediate children list of this object, or `null` if there is no Object at this position.

getChildIndex.haxe_doc: Return the index of the object `o` within the immediate children list of this object, or `-1` if it is not part of the children list.

getObjectByName.haxe_doc: Search for an object recursively by name, return `null` if not found.

iterator.haxe_doc: Return an iterator over this object immediate children

contentChanged.haxe_doc: Advanced usage Called by the children of a container object if they have `parentContainer` defined in them. Primary use-case is when the child size got changed, requiring content to reevaluate positioning such as `Flow` layouts, but also can be used for other purposes.

constraintSize.haxe_doc: Advanced usage This can be called by a parent container to constraint the size of its children. Negative value mean that constraint is to be disabled. For example, `Text` constraints it's maximum width, causing word-wrap to occur within constrained area. @see `FlowProperties.constraint`

new.haxe_doc: Create a new empty object. @param parent An optional parent `h2d.Object` instance to which Object adds itself if set.

class.haxe_doc:
A base 2D class that all scene tree elements inherit from.
Serves as a virtual container that does not display anything but can contain other objects so the various transforms are inherited to its children.
Private events `Object.onAdd`, `Object.onRemove` and `Object.onHierarchyMoved` can be used to capture when Object is added/removed from the currently active scene as well as being moved withing the object tree.
Object exposes a number of properties to control position, scale and rotation of the Object relative to its parent, but they are used indirectly during rendering. Instead, they are being used to calculate the absolute matrix transform relative to the Scene. As optimization, it's not recalculated as soon as properties are modified and delayed until `Object.sync`. Absolute object position can be accessed through private variables `Object.matA`, `Object.matB`, `Object.matC`, `Object.matD`, `Object.absX` and `Object.absY`. But it should be noted that in order to ensure up-to-date values, it's advised to call `Object.syncPos` before accessing them.

color.haxe_doc: The color multiplier for the drawable. Can be used to adjust individually each of the four channels R,G,B,A (default [1,1,1,1])

smooth.haxe_doc:
By enabling smoothing, scaling the object up or down will use hardware bilinear filtering resulting in a less crisp aspect.
By default smooth is `null` in which case `Scene.defaultSmooth` value is used.

tileWrap.haxe_doc:
Enables texture uv wrap for this Drawable, causing tiles with uv exceeding the texture size to repeat instead of clamping on edges.
Note that `tileWrap` does not use the `Tile` region as a wrapping area but instead uses underlying `h3d.mat.Texture` size. This is due to implementation specifics, as it just sets the `Texture.wrap` to either `Repeat` or `Clamp`. Because of that, proper Tile tiling can be expected only when the tile covers an entire Texture area.

colorKey.haxe_doc: Setting a colorKey color value will discard all pixels that have this exact color in the tile.

colorMatrix.haxe_doc: Setting a colorMatrix will apply a color transformation. See also `adjustColor`.

colorAdd.haxe_doc: Setting colorAdd will add the amount of color of each channel R,G,B,A to the object pixels.

adjustColor.haxe_doc: Set the `Drawable.colorMatrix` value by specifying which effects to apply. Calling `adjustColor()` without arguments will reset the colorMatrix to `null`.

getShader.haxe_doc: Returns the first shader of the given shader class among the drawable shaders. @param stype The class of the shader to look up.

getShaders.haxe_doc: Returns an iterator of all drawable shaders

addShader.haxe_doc:
Add a shader to the drawable shaders.
Keep in mind, that as stated before, drawable children do not inherit Drawable properties, which includes shaders.

removeShader.haxe_doc: Remove a shader from the drawable shaders, returns true if found or false if it was not part of our shaders.

new.haxe_doc: Create a new Drawable instance with given parent. @param parent An optional parent `h2d.Object` instance to which Drawable adds itself if set.

class.haxe_doc:
A base class for all 2D objects that will draw something on the screen.
Unlike Object base class, all properties of Drawable only apply to the current object and are not inherited by its children.

tile.haxe_doc: The tile to display. See `h2d.Tile` documentation for details. If the tile is null, a pink 5x5 bitmap will be displayed instead.

width.haxe_doc:
If set, rescale the tile to match the given width, keeping the aspect ratio unless `height` is also set.
Note that both `width` and `height` are `null` by default and in order to retrieve bitmap dimensions with scaling accurately, call `getSize` method or address `tile.width/height` to get unscaled dimensions.

height.haxe_doc:
If set, rescale the tile to match the given height, keeping the aspect ratio unless `width` is also set.
Note that both `width` and `height` are `null` by default and in order to retrieve bitmap dimensions with scaling accurately, call `getSize` method or address `tile.width/height` to get unscaled dimensions.

class.haxe_doc:
Displays a single bitmap Tile on the screen.
It is a most primitive Drawable and easiest to use, but vastly inferior to others in terms of performance when used for rendering of many tiles. When dealing with many images at once, it is recommended to use batched renderers, like `h2d.SpriteBatch` or `h2d.TileGroup`.

x.haxe_doc: The X component.

y.haxe_doc: The Y component.

dot4.haxe_doc: Returns the dot product of the 4 components with `v`.

dot3.haxe_doc: Returns the dot product of the X, Y and Z components with `v`.

scale3.haxe_doc: Multiplies the X, Y and Z components by `f`.

sub.haxe_doc: Returns `this - v` (4 components) as a new vector.

add.haxe_doc: Returns `this + v` (4 components) as a new vector.

equals.haxe_doc: Tells if all the components are equal to those of `v`.

cross.haxe_doc: Returns the cross product of the X, Y and Z components (left-handed), with W set to 1.

set.haxe_doc: Sets the components (W is 1 by default).

load.haxe_doc: Copies the components of `v`.

lerp.haxe_doc: Sets the 4 components to the linear interpolation between `v1` and `v2` (`k` from `0` to `1`).

transform.haxe_doc: Transforms the 4 components by the matrix `m`.

transformed.haxe_doc: Returns a copy of the vector with its 4 components transformed by `m`.

transform3x4.haxe_doc: Transforms the vector by `m`, ignoring the last column of the matrix (W is unchanged).

transformed3x4.haxe_doc: Returns a copy transformed by `m`, ignoring the last column of the matrix (W is set to 1).

transform3x3.haxe_doc: Transforms the X, Y and Z components by the rotation and scale of `m`.

transformed3x3.haxe_doc: Returns a copy with its X, Y and Z components transformed by the rotation and scale of `m`.

clone.haxe_doc: Returns a copy of the vector.

toVector.haxe_doc: Returns a `Vector` with the X, Y and Z components.

toString.haxe_doc: Returns a string representation of the components.

project.haxe_doc: Transforms the vector by the projection matrix `m` and divides by the resulting W (perspective division).

setColor.haxe_doc: Sets the color from an integer in `0xAARRGGBB` format (components from `0` to `1`).

makeColor.haxe_doc: Sets the color from a hue (in radians), a saturation and a brightness (HSL), from `0` to `1`.

toColor.haxe_doc: Returns the color as an integer in `0xAARRGGBB` format (alpha is `0xFF` for a `Vector`).

toColorHSL.haxe_doc: Returns the hue (`0` to `1`), saturation and lightness of the color.

toColorHSV.haxe_doc: Returns the hue (`0` to `1`), saturation and value of the color.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a vector with the given components (W is 1 by default).

class.haxe_doc: A 4 floats vector. Everytime a Vector is returned, it means a copy is created.

parseString.haxe_doc: Parses a string or an identifier.

parseColor.haxe_doc: Parses a color, as an ARGB integer: `#RGB`, `#RRGGBB`, `rgb(r,g,b)`, `rgba(r,g,b,a)`, CSS color names, `darken(c,10%)`, `lighten(c,10%)`, `saturate(c,10%)`, `desaturate(c,10%)`, and `color alpha`.

parseArray.haxe_doc: Parses values separated by spaces, with `elt`.

parsePath.haxe_doc: Parses a path: a string, an identifier or `url(path)`.

parseAuto.haxe_doc: Returns `null` for `auto`, or parses the value with `either`.

parseNone.haxe_doc: Returns `null` for `none`, or parses the value with `either`.

parseFloatPercent.haxe_doc: Parses a number, or a percentage as a ratio (`50%` is `0.5`).

parseXY.haxe_doc: Parses two numbers, as `{ x, y }`.

parseBox.haxe_doc: Parses 1 to 4 integers as `{ top, right, bottom, left }`, like the CSS `padding`.

parseGenBox.haxe_doc: Parses 1 to 4 values with `f`, as `{ top, right, bottom, left }`, like the CSS `padding`.

makeEnumParser.haxe_doc: Returns a parser of the constructors of the enum, in CSS casing (`TopLeft` is `top-left`) or lower case.

class.haxe_doc: Converts CSS values to property values: the `parseXxx` methods are used by the `@:p(xxx)` fields (`@:p(color)` uses `parseColor`). Extend it to add parsers, and set it with `@:parser` or `domkit.Macros.setDefaultParser`. The methods throw `Property.InvalidProperty` for invalid values.

adjustSdfParams.haxe_doc: Called with the SDF parameters of a font before it is loaded, to adjust them.

NULL_BG.expr: { color : 0xFFFFFF, borderL : 0, borderR : 0, borderT : 0, borderB : 0, tile : null }

m.e: { color : 0xFFFFFF, borderL : 0, borderR : 0, borderT : 0, borderB : 0, tile : null }

parseResource.haxe_doc: Parses a resource path (`url("path")` or a string) and loads it.

parseTile.haxe_doc: Parses a tile: `none`, a color, `color width height`, a resource path, or `tile("path", size)`, `tile("path", w, h)`, `grid("path", hsplit, vsplit)`, `hgrid("path", n)`, `vgrid("path", n)` for a part of an image.

parseTilePos.haxe_doc: Parses a tile position in a grid: `default`, an index, or `x y`.

parseAlign.haxe_doc: Parses an alignment: `auto`, a single horizontal or vertical alignment, or both.

parseFont.haxe_doc: Parses a font: `default`, a font resource path, or a group of fonts with `group(...)`. The path can be followed by `offset(...)`, `line-height(...)`, `base-line(...)`, then by the SDF parameters: size, channel (`alpha`, `red`, `green`, `blue` or `multi`), cutoff and smoothing.

parseTextShadow.haxe_doc: Parses a text shadow: `none`, a color, or `dx dy [color [alpha]]`.

parseFlowBackground.haxe_doc: Parses a flow background: `transparent`, `tile width height` or `tile left top right bottom` (scale grid borders), `color alpha`, or `disc(color [alpha])`.

parseCursor.haxe_doc: Parses a cursor: `default`, `button`, `move`, `textinput`, `hide`, `none`, or a resize cursor (`ns-resize`, `ew-resize`, `nwse-resize`, `nesw-resize`).

parseFilter.haxe_doc: Parses a filter: `none`, `nothing`, `grayscale(...)`, `saturate(...)`, `hue(...)`, `brightness(...)`, `outline(size, color)`, `glow(...)`, `blur(radius)`, or several of them to combine.

transitionColorAdjust.haxe_doc: Interpolates two color adjustments, for CSS transitions.

parseColorAdjust.haxe_doc: Parses a color adjustment: `none`, or one or several of `hue-rotate(...)`, `contrast(...)`, `gain(color, alpha)`, `brightness(...)`, `saturate(...)`.

parseAngleRad.haxe_doc: Parses an angle (with a `rad` or `deg` unit, radians by default) and returns it in radians.

parseAngleDeg.haxe_doc: Parses an angle (with a `rad` or `deg` unit, degrees by default) and returns it in degrees.

parseTagDefinitions.haxe_doc: Parses the HTML text tag definitions: `name("font")`, `name(color)` or `name("font", color)`.

parseMargin.haxe_doc: Parses a margin: a number, or `ignore-parent` to ignore the padding of the parent flow (see `h2d.Flow.PADDING_IGNORE_PARENT`).

parseMarginBox.haxe_doc: Parses the margins of the 4 sides, with the CSS box syntax.

class.haxe_doc: The parser of the CSS values of the h2d components (tiles, fonts, filters, alignments...).

Max.haxe_doc: The output color is the max of the source and dest colors. The blend parameters Src and Dst are ignored for this equation. `Out = MAX( Src, Dst )`

Min.haxe_doc: The output color is the min of the source and dest colors. The blend parameters Src and Dst are ignored for this equation. `Out = MAX( Src, Dst )`

enum.haxe_doc: The blending rules when rendering a Tile/Material.

PADDING_IGNORE_PARENT.haxe_doc: A special padding value for the properties of a child (`FlowProperties.paddingLeft` and others): the child ignores the padding of the flow on this side and extends to its border.

needReflow.haxe_doc:
If some sub element gets resized, you need to set reflow to true in order to force the reflow of elements. You can also directly call `Flow.reflow` which will immediately update all elements positions.
If a reflow is needed, `Flow.reflow` will be called before rendering the flow. Each change in one of the flow properties or addition/removal of elements will set needReflow to true.

horizontalAlign.haxe_doc: Horizontal alignment of elements inside the flow. See `FlowAlign` for more details.

verticalAlign.haxe_doc: Vertical alignment of elements inside the flow. See `FlowAlign` for more details.

minWidth.haxe_doc: Ensures that Flow is at least the specified outer width at all times when not null.

minHeight.haxe_doc: Ensures that Flow is at least the specified outer height at all times when not null.

maxWidth.haxe_doc: Attempts to limit the Flow outer width to the specified width. Used as a baseline for overflow when `Flow.multiline` is enabled and `Flow.layout` is `Horizontal`.

maxHeight.haxe_doc: Attempts to limit the Flow outer height to the specified height. Used as a baseline for overflow when `Flow.multiline` is enabled and `Flow.layout` is `Vertical`.

lineHeight.haxe_doc: Sets the minimum row height when `Flow.layout` is `Horizontal`.

colWidth.haxe_doc: Sets the minimum colum width when `Flow.layout` is `Vertical`.

overflow.haxe_doc: Enabling overflow will treat maxWidth/maxHeight and lineHeight/colWidth constraints as absolute : bigger elements will overflow instead of expanding the limit. See respective `FlowOverflow` values for more details.

paddingHorizontal.haxe_doc:
Will set `Flow.paddingLeft` and `Flow.paddingRight` to the given value.
Note that padding is applied inside the flow boundaries and included in the size constraint, shrinking available space for Flow children.

paddingVertical.haxe_doc:
Will set `Flow.paddingTop` and `Flow.paddingBottom` to the given value.
Note that padding is applied inside the flow boundaries and included in the size constraint, shrinking available space for Flow children.

paddingLeft.haxe_doc:
Sets the extra padding along the left edge of the Flow.
Note that padding is applied inside the flow boundaries and included in the size constraint, shrinking available space for Flow children.

paddingRight.haxe_doc:
Sets the extra padding along the right edge of the Flow.
Note that padding is applied inside the flow boundaries and included in the size constraint, shrinking available space for Flow children.

paddingTop.haxe_doc:
Sets the extra padding along the top edge of the Flow.
Note that padding is applied inside the flow boundaries and included in the size constraint, shrinking available space for Flow children.

paddingBottom.haxe_doc:
Sets the extra padding along the bottom edge of the Flow.
Note that padding is applied inside the flow boundaries and included in the size constraint, shrinking available space for Flow children.

horizontalSpacing.haxe_doc: The horizontal separation spacing between two flowed elements.

verticalSpacing.haxe_doc: The vertical separation spacing between two flowed elements.

enableInteractive.haxe_doc:
Adds an `h2d.Interactive` to the Flow that is accessible through `Flow.interactive` field. This Interactive is automatically resized to cover the whole Flow area.
Flow is added as a bottom-most (after the `Flow.backgroundTile`) child as to not impede flow elements with Interactives.

backgroundTile.haxe_doc:
Setting a background tile will create an `h2d.ScaleGrid` background which uses the `Flow.borderWidth`/`Flow.borderHeigh` values for its borders.
It will automatically resize when the reflow is done to cover the whole Flow area.

innerWidth.haxe_doc:
Calculate the client width, which is the inner size of the flow without the borders and padding.
@see `Flow.padding`

innerHeight.haxe_doc:
Calculate the client height, which is the inner size of the flow without the borders and padding.
@see `Flow.padding`

outerWidth.haxe_doc:
Flow total width. Compared to `Flow.innerWidth`, it also includes paddings and, if enabled, borders (see `Flow.borderWidth`).
@see `Flow.padding`

outerHeight.haxe_doc:
Flow total height Compared to `Flow.innerHeight`, it also includes paddings and, if enabled, borders (see `Flow.borderHeight`).
@see `Flow.padding`

layout.haxe_doc: The Flow item layout rules. See `FlowLayout` for specific details on each mode.

isInline.haxe_doc: When isInline is set to false, the flow size will be reported based on its bounds instead of its calculated size. @see `Object.getSize`

debug.haxe_doc: When set to true, the Flow will display a debug overlay. * Red box around the flow * Green box for the client space. * Blue boxes for each element. When set to false, this will disable the ability to debug the flow.

multiline.haxe_doc: When set to true, uses specified lineHeight/colWidth instead of maxWidth/maxHeight for alignment.

reverse.haxe_doc:
When set to true, children are aligned in reverse order.
Note that it does not affect render ordering, and may cause overlap of elements due to them positioned in reverse order.

fillWidth.haxe_doc: When set to true, if a width constraint is present and `minWidth` is null - Flow will expand to fill all the available horizontal space

fillHeight.haxe_doc: When set to true, if a height constraint is present and `minHeight` is null - Flow will expand to fill all the available vertical space

scrollBar.haxe_doc: The scroll bar component created when `overflow` is set to `Scroll`

scrollBarCursor.haxe_doc: The scroll bar cursor component created when `overflow` is set to `Scroll`

scrollWheelSpeed.haxe_doc: The amount of scrolling that is done when using mouse wheel (in pixels).

scrollPosY.haxe_doc: The current scrolling position for the flow content (in pixels). Only applies when overflow is Scroll or Hidden.

getProperties.haxe_doc:
Get the per-element properties. Returns null if the element is not currently part of the Flow.
Requesting the properties will cause a reflow regardless if properties values were changed or not.

addSpacing.haxe_doc:
Adds some spacing by either increasing the padding of the latest non-absolute element or the padding of the flow if there are no elements in it.
The padding affected depends on the `Flow.layout` mode. It's impossible to add spacing with a `Stack` Flow layout.

scrollIntoView.haxe_doc: Scrolls the flow vertically so that the element is visible. Returns `false` if the flow is not scrollable (see `overflow`).

makeBackground.haxe_doc: Creates the background of the flow for the tile, a `ScaleGrid` using the borders of the flow. Can be overridden to use another kind of background.

reflow.haxe_doc: Call to force all flowed elements position to be updated. See `Flow.needReflow` for more information.

onBeforeReflow.haxe_doc: Sent at the start of the `Flow.reflow`.

new.haxe_doc: Create a new Flow instance. @param parent An optional parent `h2d.Object` instance to which Flow adds itself if set.

class.haxe_doc: An automatic layout system.
The `<flow>` domkit component (`h2d.Flow`): adds the size constraints, background, layout, padding, spacing, alignment and overflow.

Horizontal.haxe_doc:
Children are aligned horizontally from left to right (or right to left when `Flow.reverse` is enabled).
If `Flow.multiline` is enabled - children can overflow to the next row if there is not enough space available within the Flow size constraints.
`Flow.lineHeight` can be used to set a fixed row height when `Flow.overflow` is set to `Limit` or `Hidden`. Objects with height that exceed the limitation will be aligned according to `Flow.verticalAlign` value vertically with `null` being treated as `Bottom`.

Vertical.haxe_doc:
Children are aligned vertically from top to bottom (or bottom to top when `Flow.reverse` is enabled).
If `Flow.multiline` is enabled - children can overflow to the next column if there is not enough space available within the Flow size constraints.
`Flow.colWidth` can be used to set a fixed column width when `Flow.overflow` is set to `Limit` or `Hidden`. Objects with height that exceed the limitation will be aligned according to `Flow.horizontalAlign` value horizontally with `null` being treated as `Left`.

Stack.haxe_doc: Children are aligned independently (`Flow.reverse` has no effect).

enum.haxe_doc: The `Flow.layout` type.

Expand.haxe_doc: Children larger than `Flow.maxWidth` / `Flow.maxHeight` will expand the flow size.

Limit.haxe_doc:
Limits the bounds reported by the flow using `Flow.maxWidth` or `Flow.maxHeight`, if set.
Children larger than max size will draw outside of the Flow bounds or overflow if `Flow.multiline` is enabled.

Hidden.haxe_doc:
Limits the bounds reported by the flow using `Flow.maxWidth` or `Flow.maxHeight`, if set.
Compared to `Limit` - Flow will mask out the content that is outside of Flow bounds.

Scroll.haxe_doc: Similar to `Hidden` but allows to scroll using `Flow.scroll*` properties for control.

enum.haxe_doc: The `Flow.overflow` rules.

ResizeNWSE.haxe_doc: A diagonal resize cursor, from top left to bottom right.

ResizeNESW.haxe_doc: A diagonal resize cursor, from top right to bottom left.

Custom.haxe_doc: A custom cursor made of bitmaps.

Callback.haxe_doc: When this cursor is selected, call the function itself, which can handle complex logic and is responsible to call hxd.System.setCursor

enum.haxe_doc: A mouse cursor (see `hxd.System.setCursor` and `h2d.Interactive.cursor`).

class.haxe_doc: The `<text>` domkit component (`h2d.Text`): adds the font, color, spacing, line breaking, alignment and shadow.
The `<html-text>` domkit component (`h2d.HtmlText`): adds the white space condensing and the tag definitions.

get.haxe_doc: Returns the default font, loaded once per engine.

class.haxe_doc: The default font embedded in Heaps.

LIVE_UPDATE.haxe_doc: If set, `watch` reloads the resources when their file changes. Enabled by default in debug builds.

name.haxe_doc: The file name of the resource, with its extension.

entry.haxe_doc: The file entry of the resource.

watch.haxe_doc: Calls `onChanged` when the file changes, if `LIVE_UPDATE` is set. Set `null` to stop watching.

to.haxe_doc: Returns the resource as the given class. Throws if it isn't an instance of it.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a resource for the file entry.

class.haxe_doc: The base class of all the resources loaded by `hxd.res.Loader`. A resource wraps a file entry and loads it on demand.

fromBytes.haxe_doc: Creates a resource from bytes, with its own loader. The path extension is used to identify the file type.

toModel.haxe_doc: Loads the resource as a 3D model.

toTexture.haxe_doc: Loads the resource as an image and returns its texture.

toTile.haxe_doc: Loads the resource as an image and returns a tile of the whole image.

toText.haxe_doc: Returns the content of the file as text.

toImage.haxe_doc: Loads the resource as an image.

toSound.haxe_doc: Loads the resource as a sound.

toPrefab.haxe_doc: Loads the resource as a prefab.

toAnimGraph.haxe_doc: Loads the resource as an animation graph.

iterator.haxe_doc: Iterates over the files of a directory.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a resource for the file entry, loaded with `loader`.

class.haxe_doc: A resource of unknown type, as returned by `hxd.res.Loader.load`: use one of its `toXXX` methods to load it as a specific type. Iterating over it lists the files of a directory.

get.haxe_doc: Returns the file entry at the path. Throws if it does not exist (`hxd.res.NotFound` for most file systems).

exists.haxe_doc: Tells if a file or directory exists at the path.

dir.haxe_doc: Returns the entries of the directory.

delete.haxe_doc: Deletes the file. Returns `false` if it can't be deleted.

class.haxe_doc: A file system containing the resources, used by `hxd.res.Loader`. Paths are relative to its root and use `/` separators.

exists.haxe_doc: Tells if a file exists at the path.

get.haxe_doc: Returns the file entry at the path. Throws if it does not exist.

class.haxe_doc: Base class of the file systems whose files are in memory (such as the embedded files): subclasses implement `getBytes`. Directories are not supported.

currentInstance.haxe_doc: Set when initializing hxd.Res, or manually. Allows code to resolve resources without compiling hxd.Res

fs.haxe_doc: The file system containing the resources.

cleanCache.haxe_doc: Clears the cache: the next loads create new resource instances.

dir.haxe_doc: Returns the resources of a directory.

exists.haxe_doc: Tells if a file exists at the path.

load.haxe_doc: Returns the resource at the path, as an `Any` to convert with one of its `toXXX` methods. Throws if the file does not exist.

loadCache.haxe_doc: Returns the resource at the path as an instance of `c`, created once and cached.

delete.haxe_doc: Deletes the file and removes its resource from the cache.

dispose.haxe_doc: Clears the cache and disposes the file system.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a loader for the file system.

class.haxe_doc: Loads the resources of a file system and caches them by path. `hxd.Res.loader` is the default instance.

DEFAULT_RESOLVER.haxe_doc:
This value can be set to use custom type resolvers.
A type resolver finds a `Class` or `Enum` instance from a given `String`. By default, the Haxe `Type` Api is used.
A type resolver must provide two methods:
1. `resolveClass(name:String):Class<Dynamic>` is called to determine a `Class` from a class name 2. `resolveEnum(name:String):Enum<Dynamic>` is called to determine an `Enum` from an enum name
This value is applied when a new `Unserializer` instance is created. Changing it afterwards has no effect on previously created instances.

run.haxe_doc:
Unserializes `v` and returns the according value.
This is a convenience function for creating a new instance of Unserializer with `v` as buffer and calling its `unserialize()` method once.

setResolver.haxe_doc:
Sets the type resolver of `this` Unserializer instance to `r`.
If `r` is `null`, a special resolver is used which returns `null` for all input values.
See `DEFAULT_RESOLVER` for more information on type resolvers.

getResolver.haxe_doc:
Gets the type resolver of `this` Unserializer instance.
See `DEFAULT_RESOLVER` for more information on type resolvers.

unserialize.haxe_doc:
Unserializes the next part of `this` Unserializer instance and returns the according value.
This function may call `this.resolver.resolveClass` to determine a Class from a String, and `this.resolver.resolveEnum` to determine an Enum from a String.
If `this` Unserializer instance contains no more or invalid data, an exception is thrown.
This operation may fail on structurally valid data if a type cannot be resolved or if a field cannot be set. This can happen when unserializing Strings that were serialized on a different Haxe target, in which the serialization side has to make sure not to include platform-specific data.
Classes are created from `Type.createEmptyInstance`, which means their constructors are not called.

new.haxe_doc:
Creates a new Unserializer instance, with its internal buffer initialized to `buf`.
This does not parse `buf` immediately. It is parsed only when calls to `this.unserialize` are made.
Each Unserializer instance maintains its own cache.

class.haxe_doc:
The `Unserializer` class is the complement to the `Serializer` class. It parses a serialization `String` and creates objects from the contained data.
This class can be used in two ways:
- create a `new Unserializer()` instance with a given serialization String, then call its `unserialize()` method until all values are extracted - call `Unserializer.run()` to unserialize a single value from a given String
The specification of the serialization format can be found here: <https://haxe.org/manual/serialization/format>

toFont.haxe_doc:
Load and cache the font instance.
Because font instance is cached, operations like `resizeTo` should be performed on a copy of the font, to avoid affecting other text fields.

new.haxe_doc: Creates the resource for the font description file entry.

class.haxe_doc: A bitmap font: a font description file (`.fnt`, in BMFont text or XML format, or other supported formats) with its image. Use `toFont` to get the `h2d.Font`.

resolveSubFont.haxe_doc: Returns the font used by the text when its font is a group of fonts (`FontGroup`). Returns the first sub font by default: it can be replaced to select another one, such as the one of the current language.

font.haxe_doc: The font used to render text.

textColor.haxe_doc: Text RGB color. Alpha value is ignored.

maxWidth.haxe_doc:
When set, limits maximum line width and causes word-wrap. Affects positioning of the text depending on `textAlign` value.
When Text is affected by size constraints (see `Object.constraintSize`), smallest of the two is used for word-wrap.

dropShadow.haxe_doc: Adds simple drop shadow to the Text with specified offset, color and alpha. Causes text to be rendered twice (first drop shadow and then the text itself).

textWidth.haxe_doc: Calculated text width. Can exceed maxWidth in certain cases.

textHeight.haxe_doc:
Calculated text height.
Not a completely precise text metric and increments in the `Font.lineHeight` steps. In `HtmlText`, can be increased by various values depending on the active line font and `HtmlText.lineHeightMode` value.

textAlign.haxe_doc: Text align rules dictate how the text lines are positioned. See `Align` for specific details on each alignment mode.

wordBreak.haxe_doc: When `lineBreak` is enabled, allow breaking inside a word if it does not fit on a single line. Without it, a word longer than `maxWidth` overflows the text bounds.

validateText.haxe_doc:
Extra validation of the `text` variable when it's changed. Override to add custom validation.
Only validation of the text is allowed, and attempting to change the text value will lead to undefined behavior.

calcTextWidth.haxe_doc: Calculates and returns width of the provided `text` with settings this Text instance.

splitText.haxe_doc: Perform a word-wrap of the `text` based on this Text settings.

splitRawText.haxe_doc: Advanced usage Perform a word-wrap of the text based on this Text settings. @param text String to word-wrap. @param leftMargin Starting x offset of the first line. @param afterData Minimum remaining space required at the end of the line. @param font Optional overriding font to use instead of currently set. @param sizes Optional line width array. Will be populated with sizes of split lines if present. Sizes will include both `leftMargin` in it's first line entry. @param prevChar Optional character code for concatenation purposes (proper kernings).

getTextProgress.haxe_doc: Returns cut `text` based on `progress` percentile. Can be used to gradually show appearing text. (Especially useful when using `HtmlText`)

setColorSegments.haxe_doc: Set the text color segments. This is an Array containing a pair of (position,color). Each time the text display will reach the given position, the color will be set. The segment color is multiplied by the global textColor.

class.haxe_doc:
A basic text renderer with multiline support.
See [Text](https://github.com/HeapsIO/heaps/wiki/Text) section of the manual for more details.

defaultLoadImage.haxe_doc: A default method HtmlText uses to load images for `` tag. See `HtmlText.loadImage` for details.

defaultLoadFont.haxe_doc: A default method HtmlText uses to load fonts for `<font>` tags with `face` attribute. See `HtmlText.loadFont` for details.

defaultFormatText.haxe_doc: A default method HtmlText uses to format assigned text. See `HtmlText.formatText` for details.

defineDefaultHtmlTag.haxe_doc: Associate a custom html tag to a specific font and color.

condenseWhite.haxe_doc: When enabled, condenses extra spaces (carriage-return, line-feed, tabulation and space character) to one space. If not set, uncondensed whitespace is left as is, as well as line-breaks.

propagateInteractiveNode.haxe_doc: When enabled, nodes that create interactives will propagate events

imageSpacing.haxe_doc: The spacing after `` tags in pixels.

lineHeightMode.haxe_doc: Line height calculation mode controls how much space lines take up vertically. Changing mode to `Constant` restores the legacy behavior of HtmlText.

imageVerticalAlign.haxe_doc: Vertical alignment of the images in `` tag relative to the text.

loadImage.haxe_doc: Method that should return an `h2d.Tile` instance for `` tags. By default calls `HtmlText.defaultLoadImage` method. HtmlText does not cache tile instances. Due to internal structure, method should be deterministic and always return same Tile on consequent calls with same `url` input. @param url A value contained in `src` attribute.

formatText.haxe_doc: Called when text is assigned, allowing to process arbitrary text to a valid XHTML.

defineHtmlTag.haxe_doc: Define a custom html tag to be displayed with specific font and color.

defineHtmlTags.haxe_doc: Define or reset a set of custom html tags to be displayed with specific font and color.

class.haxe_doc:
A simple HTML text renderer.
See the [Text](https://github.com/HeapsIO/heaps/wiki/Text) section of the manual for more details and a list of the supported HTML tags.

Left.haxe_doc: Aligns the text to the left edge.

Right.haxe_doc:
Aligns the text to the right edge.
When `Text.maxWidth` is set and/or Text size is constrained (see `Object.constraintSize`), right edge is considered the smallest of the two.
Otherwise edge is at the `0` coordinate of the Text instance.
See Text sample for showcase.

Center.haxe_doc:
Centers the text alignment.
When `Text.maxWidth` is set and/or Text size is constrained (see `Object.constraintSize`), center is calculated from 0 to the smallest of the two.
Otherwise text is centered around `0` coordinate of the Text instance.
See Text sample for showcase.

MultilineRight.haxe_doc:
With respect to Text constraints, aligns the text to the right edge of the longest line width.
When `Text.maxWidth` is set and/or Text size is constrained (see `Object.constraintSize`), right edge is calculated as the smallest value of the `maxWidth`, constrained width and longest line width (after word-wrap from constraints).
Otherwise uses longest line width as the right edge.
See Text sample for showcase.

MultilineCenter.haxe_doc:
Centers the text with respect to Text constraints with the longest line width.
When `Text.maxWidth` is set and/or Text size is constrained (see `Object.constraintSize`), center is calculated from the to the smallest value of the `maxWidth`, constrained width and longest line width (after word-wrap from constraints).
Otherwise calculates center from 0 to the longest line width.
See Text sample for showcase.

enum.haxe_doc: `Text` alignment rules.

class.haxe_doc: The `<input>` domkit component (`h2d.TextInput`): adds the width, the cursor and selection tiles, the edition, background color and multiline options.

showSoftwareKeyboard.haxe_doc: Called when a text input gets the focus, if `useSoftwareKeyboard` is set. Replace it to display the virtual keyboard of the platform.

hideSoftwareKeyboard.haxe_doc: Called when a text input loses the focus. Replace it to hide the virtual keyboard of the platform.

cursorIndex.haxe_doc: Current position of the input cursor. When TextInput is not focused value is -1.

cursorTile.haxe_doc: The Tile used to render the input cursor.

selectionTile.haxe_doc: The Tile used to render the background for selected text. When rendering, this Tile is stretched horizontally to fill entire selection area.

cursorBlinkTime.haxe_doc: The blinking interval of the cursor in seconds.

inputWidth.haxe_doc: Maximum input width. Contrary to `Text.maxWidth` does not cause a word-wrap, but also masks out contents that are outside the max width.

multiline.haxe_doc: Whether the text input allows multiple lines.

selectionRange.haxe_doc: If not null, represents current text selection range.

canEdit.haxe_doc: When disabled, user would not be able to edit the input text (selection is still available).

backgroundColor.haxe_doc: If set, TextInput will render provided color as a background to text interactive area.

insertTabs.haxe_doc: If set, insert these characters when pressing Tab

useSoftwareKeyboard.haxe_doc: When disabled, showSoftwareKeyboard will not be called.

onSoftwareKeyboardEnd.haxe_doc: To be called by the platform integration when the virtual keyboard is closed, with `isSubmit` set if the text was validated.

getTextPos.haxe_doc: When lineBreak is enabled and some word wrapping operation applies, the cursorIndex no longer represent the position in the exact text but in the wrapped text, including inserted newlines. This function allows to translate the cursor position into the position into the text. Use getCursorPos to convert the text position into a cursor position.

getCursorLine.haxe_doc: Convert a text line number into a display line number. First line is 0. See getTextPos() and getCursorPos().

isWordLimit.haxe_doc: This function is used to code the behavior of Ctrl-Left/Right word skipping. By default it uses charset.isSpace but can be customized.

loadState.haxe_doc: Load the state from a previous input, copy the current text, cursor position, selection etc. This allows to continue uninterrupted input experience while the input component has been reset/rebuild

clearUndo.haxe_doc: Clears the undo and redo history.

getTextLength.haxe_doc: The expanded text length, including inserted line breaks.

getSelectedText.haxe_doc: Returns a String representing currently selected text area or `null` if no text is selected.

blur.haxe_doc: Removes the focus from the text input.

hasFocus.haxe_doc: Checks if TextInput is currently focused.

onSubmit.haxe_doc: Triggered when a not multiline text input is validated with Enter

onChange.haxe_doc: Sent when user modifies TextInput contents.

class.haxe_doc:
A skinnable text input handler.
Supports text selection, keyboard cursor navigation, as well as basic hotkeys: `Ctrl + Z`, `Ctrl + Y` for undo and redo and `Ctrl + A` to select all text.

propagateEvents.haxe_doc: If set, events are also sent to the interactives below this one.

cursor.haxe_doc: The cursor displayed when the mouse is over the interactive.

handleEvent.haxe_doc: Handles an event sent to the interactive.

getInteractiveScene.haxe_doc: Returns the scene of the interactive.

class.haxe_doc: An object which can receive events from `SceneEvents`, such as `h2d.Interactive` and `h3d.scene.Interactive`.

width.haxe_doc: Width of the Interactive. Ignored if `Interactive.shape` is set.

height.haxe_doc: Height of the Interactive. Ignored if `Interactive.shape` is set.

cursor.haxe_doc: Cursor used when Interactive is under mouse cursor.

isEllipse.haxe_doc: Performs an elliptic hit-test instead of rectangular one based on `Interactive.width` and `height`. Ignored if `Interactive.shape` is set.

enableRightButton.haxe_doc: When enabled, interacting with secondary mouse buttons (right button/wheel) will cause `onPush`, `onClick`, `onRelease` and `onReleaseOutside` callbacks. Otherwise those callbacks will only be triggered with primary mouse button (left button).

allowMultiClick.haxe_doc: When enabled, allows to receive several onClick events the same frame.

backgroundColor.haxe_doc: If set, Interactive will draw a `Tile` with `[width, height]` dimensions of specified color (including alpha).

shape.haxe_doc: Detailed shape collider for Interactive. If set, `width` and `height` properties are ignored for collision checks.

shapeX.haxe_doc: Detailed shape X offset from Interactive.

shapeY.haxe_doc: Detailed shape Y offset from Interactive.

preventClick.haxe_doc: Reset current pressed state of the Interactive, preventing the `onClick` or `onReleaseOutside` being triggered when user releases mouse button.

focus.haxe_doc: Sets focus on this `Interactive`. If Interactive was not already focused and it receives focus - `onFocus` event is sent. Interactive won't become focused if during `onFocus` call it will set `Event.cancel` to `true`.

blur.haxe_doc: Removes focus from interactive if it's focused. If Interactive is currently focused - `onFocusLost` event will be sent. Interactive won't lose focus if during `onFocusLost` call it will set `Event.cancel` to `true`.

isOver.haxe_doc: Checks if Interactive is currently hovered by the mouse.

hasFocus.haxe_doc: Checks if Interactive is currently focused.

onOver.haxe_doc:
Sent when mouse enters Interactive hitbox area.
`Event.propagate` and `Event.cancel` are ignored during `onOver`. Propagation can be set with `onMove` event, as well as cancelling `onMove` will prevent `onOver`.

onOut.haxe_doc: Sent when mouse exits Interactive hitbox area. `Event.propagate` and `Event.cancel` are ignored during `onOut`.

onPush.haxe_doc: Sent when Interactive is pressed by the user.

onRelease.haxe_doc:
Sent when Interactive is unpressed under multiple circumstances. * Always sent if user releases mouse while it is inside Interactive hitbox area. This happens regardless if that Interactive was pressed prior or not, and due to that it's not guaranteed that `Interactive.onPush` would precede this event. `Event.kind` is set to `ERelease` during this event. * Sent before `Interactive.onReleaseOutside` if this Interactive was pressed, but released outside its hitbox area. `Event.kind` is set to `EReleaseOutside` during this event.
See `Interactive.onClick` and `Interactive.onReleaseOutside` methods for separate events that trigger only when user interacts with this particular Interactive.

onReleaseOutside.haxe_doc:
Sent when user presses the Interactive, moves the mouse outside its hitbox area and releases the mouse button.
Can be prevented to fire by calling `Interactive.preventClick` during or after `Interactive.onPush` event.
`Interactive.onRelease` is sent with `Event.kind` being `EReleaseOutside` just before this event.

onClick.haxe_doc:
Sent when the Interactive is clicked by the user.
Can be prevented to fire by calling `Interactive.preventClick` during or after `Interactive.onPush` event.
`Interactive.onRelease` is sent with `Event.kind` being `ERelease` just before this event.

onMove.haxe_doc:
Sent when user moves within the Interactive hitbox area. See `Interactive.onCheck` for event when user does not move the mouse.
Cancelling the `Event` will prevent interactive from becoming overed, causing `Interactive.onOut` if it was overed previously. Interactive would be treated as not overed as long as event is cancelled even if mouse is within the hitbox area.

onWheel.haxe_doc: Sent when user scrolls mouse wheel above the Interactive. Wheel delta can be obtained through the `Event.wheelDelta`.

onFocus.haxe_doc:
Sent when Interactive receives focus during `Interactive.focus` call.
Cancelling the `Event` will prevent the Interactive from becoming focused.

onFocusLost.haxe_doc:
Sent when Interactive lost focus either via `Interactive.blur` call or when user clicks on another Interactive/outside this Interactive hitbox area.
Cancelling the `Event` will prevent the Interactive from losing focus.

onKeyUp.haxe_doc: Sent when this Interactive is focused and user unpressed a keyboard key. Unpressed key can be accessed through `Event.keyCode`.

onKeyDown.haxe_doc: Sent when this Interactive is focused and user pressed a keyboard key. Pressed key can be accessed through `Event.keyCode`.

onCheck.haxe_doc:
Sent every frame when user hovers an Interactive but does not move the mouse. See `Interactive.onMove` for event when user moves the mouse.
Cancelling the `Event` will prevent interactive from becoming overed, causing `Interactive.onOut` if it was overed previously. Interactive would be treated as not overed as long as event is cancelled even if mouse is within the hitbox area.

onTextInput.haxe_doc: Sent when this Interactive is focused and user inputs text. Character added can be accessed through `Event.charCode`.

class.haxe_doc:
A user input handler.
Hitbox area can be a rectangle, an ellipse or an arbitrary shape (`h2d.col.Collider`).
Note that Interactive does not reports its hitbox bounds in `Object.getBounds` unless `Interactive.backgroundColor` is set, in which case `width` and `height` are reported.
By default, Interactive only reacts to primary (left) mouse button for actions, see `Interactive.enableRightButton` for details.

EPush.haxe_doc: A mouse button or a touch is pressed.

ERelease.haxe_doc: A mouse button or a touch is released.

EMove.haxe_doc: The mouse or a touch moves.

EReleaseOutside.haxe_doc: A button pressed on an interactive is released outside of it.

ECheck.haxe_doc: Used to check if we are still on the interactive if no EMove was triggered this frame.

enum.haxe_doc: The kinds of `Event`.

class.haxe_doc: The `<mask>` domkit component (`h2d.Mask`): adds the mask width and height.

unmask.haxe_doc: Unmasks the previously masked area from `Mask.maskWith`. @param ctx The render context to unmask.

width.haxe_doc: The width of the masked area.

height.haxe_doc: The height of the masked area.

scrollX.haxe_doc: Horizontal scroll offset of the Mask content in pixels. Can be clamped by `Mask.scrollBounds`.

scrollY.haxe_doc: Vertical scroll offset of the Mask content in pixels. Can be clamped by `Mask.scrollBounds`.

scrollBounds.haxe_doc: Optional scroll boundaries that prevent content from overscroll.

scrollTo.haxe_doc: Scroll the Mask content to the specified offset.

scrollBy.haxe_doc: Scroll the Mask content by the specified offset relative to the current scroll offset.

class.haxe_doc:
Restricts rendering area within the `[width, height]` rectangle. For more advanced masking, see `h2d.filter.AbstractMask`.
Rotation of the mask does not rotate the masked area and instead causes it to cover the bounding box of the mask.
The `Mask.maskWidth` and `Mask.unmask` can be used to mask out rendering area without direct usage of Mask instance in-between.
The `<scale-grid>` domkit component (`h2d.ScaleGrid`): adds the borders, their scale and tiling, and the size.

tile.haxe_doc: The reference tile used as a Texture source to draw.

rangeMin.haxe_doc: If set, only tiles indexed above or equal to `rangeMin` will be drawn.

rangeMax.haxe_doc: If set, only tiles indexed below `rangeMax` will be drawn.

clear.haxe_doc: Clears all TileGroup contents and disposes allocated GPU memory.

invalidate.haxe_doc: When new data is added, it's not automatically flushed to the GPU memory if it was already allocated (when TileGroup is either rendered or received `Object.sync` call), in which case call `invalidate()` to force a refresh of the GPU data.

count.haxe_doc: Returns the number of tiles added to the group.

setDefaultColor.haxe_doc: Sets the default tinting color when adding new Tiles.

class.haxe_doc:
A static Tile batch renderer.
TileGroup follows an upload-once policy and does not allow modification of the already added geometry. To add new geometry it's mandatory to call `TileGroup.invalidate`. In case existing geometry has to be modified - entire group have to be cleared with `TileGroup.clear` and repopulated from ground up.
Usage note: While TileGroup allows for multiple unique textures, each texture swap causes a new drawcall, and due to that it's recommended to minimize the amount of used textures per TileGroup instance, ideally limiting to only one texture.

borderLeft.haxe_doc: The width of the left border in pixels.

borderRight.haxe_doc: The width of the right border in pixels.

borderTop.haxe_doc: The height of the top border in pixels.

borderBottom.haxe_doc: The height of the bottom border in pixels.

borderWidth.haxe_doc: Set the width of left and right borders altogether.

borderHeight.haxe_doc: Set the height of top and bottom borders altogether.

width.haxe_doc: The width of the bitmap. Setting to values less than `borderLeft + borderRight` leads to undefined results.

height.haxe_doc: The height of the bitmap. Setting to values less than `borderTop + borderBottom` leads to undefined results.

tileBorders.haxe_doc: When enabled, borders will be repeated along the edges instead of stretching to match the desired dimensions.

tileCenter.haxe_doc: When enabled, center will be repeated along the edges instead of stretching to match the desired dimensions.

ignoreScale.haxe_doc:
When enabled, the borders will ignore the final scale of the `h2d.ScaleGrid` to be rendered pixel perfect. This does not change the values of `borderLeft`, `borderRight`, `borderTop` or `borderBottom`.
Center tile is always stretched.

borderScale.haxe_doc: Scale factor applied to borders only. If combined with `ignoreScale`, becomes an absolute scale independent from the scene scale.

class.haxe_doc:
A simple 9-slice bitmap renderer.
Enables rendering of the Tile as a stretchable surface with unscaled corners, stretched center and either stretched or tiled borders. Set `ScaleGrid.width` and `ScaleGrid.height` to resize the ScaleGrid.

buffer.haxe_doc: The primitive vertex buffer, holding its vertexes data.

indexes.haxe_doc: The primitive indexes buffer, holding its triangles indices.

refCount.haxe_doc: Current amount of references to this Primitive. Use `incref` and `decref` methods to affect this value. If it reaches 0, it will be automatically disposed.

triCount.haxe_doc: The number of triangles the primitive has.

vertexCount.haxe_doc: The number of vertexes the primitive has.

getCollider.haxe_doc: Return a local collider for the primitive

getBounds.haxe_doc: Return the bounds for the primitive

incref.haxe_doc: Increase reference count of the Primitive.

decref.haxe_doc: Decrease reference count of the Primitive. If recount reaches zero, Primitive is automatically disposed when last referencing mesh is removed from scene.

alloc.haxe_doc: Allocate the primitive on GPU. Used for internal usage.

selectMaterial.haxe_doc: Select the specified sub material before drawin. Used for internal usage.

getMaterialIndexes.haxe_doc: Returns the number and offset of indexes for the specified material

getMaterialIndexStart.haxe_doc: Returns the first index of the given material group and level of detail.

getMaterialIndexCount.haxe_doc: Returns the number of indexes of the given material group and level of detail.

render.haxe_doc: Render the primitive. Used for internal usage.

dispose.haxe_doc: Dispose the primitive, freeing the GPU memory it uses.

toString.haxe_doc: Return the primitive type.

screenRatioToLod.haxe_doc: Returns the level of detail to use for an object covering `screenRatio` of the screen (see `h3d.scene.Mesh.screenRatio`).

getCullingScreenRatio.haxe_doc: Returns the screen ratio under which the meshes using this primitive are not drawn at all (`0` to always draw them).

class.haxe_doc: h3d.prim.Primitive is the base class for all 3D primitives. You can't create an instance of it and need to use one of its subclasses.

useAllocatorLimit.haxe_doc: The buffers with fewer floats than this limit are allocated with `hxd.impl.Allocator`, the bigger ones are allocated directly.

clear.haxe_doc: Remove all data from Content instance.

isEmpty.haxe_doc: Tells if the content has no tile.

addPoint.haxe_doc:
Intended for internal usage. Adds single vertex to the buffer with no 0 uv.
Usage warning: When adding geometry trough addPoint, they should be added in groups of 4 that form a quad, and then `updateState(null, quads * 2)` should be called to ensure proper batch rendering.
Points are added in the following order: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.

flush.haxe_doc: Flushes added quads to the rendering buffer. Only flushes if rendering buffer is disposed, and to ensure new data is added, call `dispose()` first.

class.haxe_doc: TileGroup internal class for batched quad geometry rendering.

currentTexture.haxe_doc: Current active texture of the BatchDrawState. Represents the most recent texture that was set with `setTile` or `setTexture`. Always null after state initialization or after `clear` call.

totalCount.haxe_doc: A total amount of vertices added to the BatchDrawState.

setTile.haxe_doc: Switches currently active texture to one in the given `tile` if it differs and splits the render state. @param tile A Tile containing a texture that should be used for the next set of vertices. Does nothing if `null`.

setTexture.haxe_doc: Switches currently active texture to the given `texture` if it differs and splits the render state. @param texture The texture that should be used for the next set of vertices. Does nothing if `null`.

clear.haxe_doc: Resets the BatchDrawState by removing all texture references and zeroing vertex counter.

class.haxe_doc:
Automates buffer segmentation when rendering 2D geometry with multiple unique textures.
Primary use-case is to allow usage of multiple textures without the need to manually manage them. Causes extra draw call each time a texture is swapped. Due to that, for production it is recommended to combine assets in atlases for optimal performance.
Depending on geometry type, vertex count should be in groups of 4 vertices per quad or 3 indices per triangle.

texture.haxe_doc: Texture associated with draw state instance.

class.haxe_doc: The `<video>` domkit component (`h2d.Video`): adds the video resource (`src`) and looping.

videoWidth.haxe_doc: Video width. Value is undefined until video is ready to play.

videoHeight.haxe_doc: Video height. Value is undefined until video is ready to play.

time.haxe_doc: Tells current timestamp of the video.

loop.haxe_doc: When enabled, video will loop indefinitely.

onError.haxe_doc: Sent when there is an error with the decoding or playback of the video.

onEnd.haxe_doc: Sent when video playback is finished.

dispose.haxe_doc: Disposes of the currently playing Video and frees GPU memory.

class.haxe_doc: A video file playback Drawable. Due to platform specifics, each target have their own limitations. * Hashlink: Playback ability depends on `https://github.com/HeapsIO/hlvideo` library. It support only video with the AV1 codec packed into a WEBM container. * JavaScript: HTML Video element will be used. Playback is restricted by content-security policy and browser decoder capabilities.

parser.haxe_doc: Converts the CSS value to the property value. Throws `Property.InvalidProperty` if invalid.

defaultValue.haxe_doc: The value applied when no CSS rule sets the property.

apply.haxe_doc: Applies the value to an object.

transition.haxe_doc: Interpolates between two values, or `null` (floats are interpolated, other values change at the end of the transition).

class.haxe_doc: How a component handles a CSS property: parses its value, applies it to the objects of type `O`, and interpolates it for the transitions.

enum.haxe_doc: A token of the CSS lexer.

abstract.haxe_doc: The pseudo classes of a CSS selector, as bit flags.

Odd.haxe_doc: `:odd`: the children at an odd index, counting from 0.

Even.haxe_doc: `:even`: the children at an even index, counting from 0.

NotImportant.haxe_doc: `:not-important`: lowers the priority of the rule below the rules without it.

NeedChildren.haxe_doc: Set with the pseudo classes depending on the position among the parent's children.

toInt.haxe_doc: Returns the flags as an integer.

has.haxe_doc: Tells if the flag is set.

Odd.haxe_doc: `:odd`: the children at an odd index, counting from 0.

NotImportant.haxe_doc: `:not-important`: lowers the priority of the rule below the rules without it.

NeedChildren.haxe_doc: Set with the pseudo classes depending on the position among the parent's children.

toInt.haxe_doc: Returns the flags as an integer.

has.haxe_doc: Tells if the flag is set.

abstract.haxe_doc: The relation between a selector and its parent selector.
